newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Bell Telecom wins case over licence.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Bell Telecom wins case over licence.

text.p: The Philippine Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a petition by the head of the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) and paved the way for a licence for local firm Bell Telecommunications Philippines.

Bell Telecom had applied to the NTC in 1993 for a permit to offer nationwide phone services but was rejected because the NTC head Simeon Kintanar felt it did not have the financial and technical capability for such a project.
Besides Kintanar, the NTC has two other commissioners who had said Bell Telecom should be given the licence.
The Supreme Court in a decision upheld Bell Telecom's contention that the NTC was a collegial body and that the decision of the majority should have been upheld.
Bell Telecom plans to install 2.6 million telephone lines in the country within 10 years.
The company is owned by a group of local investors and if it wins a licence, it could be the first direct competititor to the Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co..
